questions.stem: Anatomy is divided into several branches to study the systems, apparatuses and organs of the human body. Which of the following correspond to descriptive anatomy?
options: The study of the location of organs
The analytical study of the morphology of separate organs
The study of the relations of organs

questions.stem: The anatomical reference position is the position on which all anatomical descriptions are based. Which of the following correspond to it?
options: Palms of the hands facing forward
Feet apart, placed on the ground

questions.stem: The paramedian sagittal plane is an anteroposterior anatomical plane that divides the body into two parts. What are its characteristics?
options: It divides the body into right and left parts
It divides the body into medial and lateral parts

questions.stem: For descriptive, topographic and functional anatomy we use reference axes: the body axis, the hand axis and the foot axis. What are the characteristics of the body axis?
options: A line dropped from the vertex
A line dropped from the shoulder
A line passing through the umbilicus
A line passing through the body's center of gravity

questions.stem: Flexion is a movement that brings a part of the body forward. What are its axis and plane?
options: A transverse axis and a sagittal plane
A sagittal axis and a frontal plane
A vertical axis and a transverse plane
A vertical axis and a sagittal plane
A transverse axis and a frontal plane

questions.stem: Cartilage belongs to the skeletal system and makes up most of the fetal skeleton. What are the characteristics of fibrous cartilage (fibrocartilage)?
options: It is rich in elastic fibers
It is rich in collagen fibers
It forms the articular adaptation structures of joints

questions.stem: The human skeleton has two parts: an axial skeleton and an appendicular skeleton. Which of the following bones belong to the axial skeleton?
The bone surface has articular and non-articular cavities; the latter give passage or attachment to anatomical elements. Which of the following correspond to non-articular cavities?
Bone is a dense, solid specialized connective tissue rich in calcium phosphate and carbonate, made of compact and spongy bone. What are the characteristics of compact bone?
options: It is made of bony trabeculae
It is made of interstitial lamellae

questions.stem: The hip bone belongs to the pelvic girdle and is formed embryologically by the junction of 3 bony pieces: ilium, ischium and pubis. Which of the following belong to its medial surface?
The hip bone has 4 borders: superior, inferior, anterior and posterior. Which of the following belong to its posterior border?
The tibial plateau is the base of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia and articulates with the femoral condyles. Which anatomical elements make it up?
options: The medial superior tibial articular surface

questions.stem: The distal epiphysis of the tibia articulates below with the talus. Which are the articular surfaces of this epiphysis?
options: The medial superior tibial articular surface
The articular surface of the medial malleolus
The articular surface of the lateral malleolus
The lateral superior tibial articular surface

questions.stem: The proximal femoral epiphysis has a femoral head, a greater trochanter, a lesser trochanter and a neck. Which of the following correspond to the greater trochanter?
The distal epiphysis of the femur articulates with the patella and the tibial plateau. Which are the articular surfaces of this epiphysis?
options: The patellar articular surface of the femur
The posterior surface of the patella

questions.stem: The radio-ulnar articular disc:
options: Is a triangular ligament spreading horizontally
Occupies the lateral third of the antebrachial articular surface
Is covered with cartilage on its 2 surfaces, superior and inferior
Gives attachment to the articular capsule on its 2 borders, anterior and posterior
Attaches laterally to the ulnar styloid process

questions.stem: Among the passive ligaments of the radiocarpal joint, which attach to the capitate?
options: The radial collateral ligament of the carpus
The ulnar collateral ligament of the carpus

questions.stem: The lateral ligament of the talocrural (ankle) joint:
options: Ends on the talus and the navicular bone
Can be injured in common ankle sprains

questions.stem: The scapulohumeral joint is the proximal joint of the upper (thoracic) limb. It is a joint that is:
options: Not very mobile and rather fragile

questions.stem: Synarthroses are immobile joints in which the bony surfaces are united by connective tissue:
options: The articular surfaces are covered with articular cartilage
The sutures of the skull are synfibroses
A gomphosis is the joint that unites a tooth to its dental socket
Synarthroses are temporary joints during growth
Syndesmoses unite articular surfaces very close to each other

questions.stem: Synovial joints are mobile joints making up most limb joints. They are characterized by:
options: Epiphyseal articular surfaces of variable shape, covered with hyaline cartilage
The synovial membrane, lining the inner surface of the capsule, is richly vascularized and innervated
Ligaments are the active stabilizers of a joint
Hyaline cartilage has a constant thickness in all joints
Tendons of periarticular muscles are passive stabilizers of the joint

questions.stem: Articular adaptation structures are fibrocartilaginous structures interposed between the articular surfaces:
options: They are of three types: labrum, meniscus and disc
They are richly innervated and vascularized
They are devoid of vessels and nerves
The menisci are fibrocartilages of the elbow
A tear of a fibrocartilage can heal

questions.stem: Muscles are organs that can contract under a stimulus; they are divided into three groups: striated, smooth and mixed. Striated muscles are:
Smooth muscles are:
options: Under control of the voluntary nervous system
Under control of the autonomic (neurovegetative) nervous system

questions.stem: Among the mixed muscles:
options: The broad muscles of the abdomen

questions.stem: The scapula is a flat triangular bone applied to the postero-superior part of the thorax. It has three borders:
Among the elements of the supero-lateral angle of the scapula:
The ulna is a long, paired bone forming the medial part of the forearm skeleton. Its proximal epiphysis shows:
options: The olecranon, a horizontal and anterior process
The olecranon, a vertical and posterior process
The coronoid process, which is horizontal and anterior
The coronoid process, which is vertical and posterior
The radial notch on its medial surface

questions.stem: The radius is a long, paired bone forming the lateral part of the forearm skeleton. Its proximal epiphysis has the radial head, made up of:
options: The radial cupula (fovea), its superior surface
The articular circumference, called the fovea
The radial cupula, which is the rim of the radial head
The articular circumference, which is the rim of the radial head
The radial tuberosity, called the bicipital tuberosity

questions.stem: The radial head:
options: The radial cupula articulates with the ulna
The articular circumference articulates with the capitulum
The radial cupula articulates with the capitulum
The articular circumference articulates with the ulna
The radial cupula articulates with the carpus

questions.stem: The distal end of the radius has five surfaces. Which statements are correct?
options: The ventral surface is hollowed by grooves
The dorsal surface is hollowed by grooves
The inferior surface is articular and triangular
The inferior surface has an articular surface with the ulna called the ulnar notch

questions.stem: The scaphoid bone is a bone:
